content: Cefuroxime axetil is an oral second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic that is FDA-approved for treating various bacterial infections. These include pharyngitis/tonsillitis, acute bacterial otitis media, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis, acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, secondary bacterial infections of acute bronchitis, uncomplicated skin and skin-structure infections, uncomplicated urinary tract infections, uncomplicated gonorrhea, early Lyme disease (erythema migrans), and impetigo. Common adverse reactions associated with cefuroxime axetil include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and vaginitis. It is important to note that cefuroxime axetil tablets and oral suspension are not bioequivalent and cannot be substituted on a milligram-per-milligram basis. Cefuroxime axetil works by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis, making it bactericidal. It retains activity in the presence of some beta-lactamases, including penicillinases and cephalosporinases, produced by both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The drug is primarily eliminated by the kidneys, and dosage adjustments are necessary for patients with a creatinine clearance of less than 30 mL/min. Cefuroxime axetil should be used cautiously in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to cephalosporins, penicillins, or other beta-lactam antibiotics due to the potential for cross-reactivity. Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents, including cefuroxime axetil. This condition can range from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. If CDAD is suspected or confirmed, discontinuation of ongoing antibiotic use not directed against C. difficile may be necessary, along with appropriate fluid and electrolyte management, protein supplementation, and antibiotic treatment of C. difficile. Prolonged use of cefuroxime axetil may lead to the overgrowth of nonsusceptible microorganisms. Additionally, cefuroxime axetil may affect gut flora, potentially reducing the efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives. Cefuroxime axetil is classified as Pregnancy Category B by the FDA. Animal studies have not shown evidence of harm to the fetus, but adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women are lacking. The drug should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Cefuroxime is excreted in human milk, so caution should be exercised when administering it to nursing mothers. In pediatric patients aged 3 months to 12 years, cefuroxime axetil oral suspension is indicated for treating mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of designated microorganisms. The safety and effectiveness of cefuroxime axetil in treating infections other than those specifically listed have not been established. Cefuroxime axetil has been shown to be effective against a range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus (methicillin-susceptible isolates only), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Haemophilus parainfluenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Patients receiving cefuroxime axetil should be monitored for potential adverse effects, including gastrointestinal disturbances, hypersensitivity reactions, and changes in prothrombin time. In cases of overdose, symptoms such as cerebral irritation, seizures, or encephalopathy may occur. Hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis can reduce serum levels of cefuroxime in such cases. Cefuroxime axetil should be prescribed only for infections proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria to reduce the development of drug-resistant organisms and maintain its effectiveness.
